what is the secure world, and what keeps apps out

cards.title: where the decisions sit
items: A10e: in the bootloader you can read
Tab A8: lk asks the secure world - Trusty judges the unlock token (cmd 0x33) and checks the image (cmd 0x20); lk sets the boot state from the answer, and skips the check when unlocked
lk runs its own libavb too, but that feeds the kernel cmdline, not the boot-state gate

cards.title: unlock
items: A10e: state read in the bootloader; OEM unlock refused on that unit
Tab A8: a token in miscdata that Trusty judges (chip-bound if its key label holds); unlocked from Download Mode, flash.locked read back 0

cards.title: the secure world and its fence
items: A10e: TEEGRIS; TrustZone nodes 0666, SELinux the only fence
Tab A8: Trusty; TEE node 0660 plus SELinux; of the HALs that touch the TEE, apps can find only the media ones, never the key ones

cards.title: why a GSI fits the tablet
items: A10e: vendor Treble level 3, below what the GSI ships
Tab A8: level 5, VNDK 30, kernel 4.14.199 - matches the LineageOS 22.2 GSI
